sentences.text: 1 This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "the Act of 1988") arises out of the award dated 08.09.2017 passed by the learned Fifth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (for short "learned Tribunal"), Bilaspur, District Bilaspur in Claim Case No. 738/2014.

entities.text: Fifth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5314 2.

Brief facts of the case are that the claimant who is the mother of the deceased have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for the death of Sonu @ Sunil Kumar on 21.09.2014 when he was driving his motorcycle bicycle and when he reached near village Seoni, the driver of the offending vehicle bus bearing registration No. CG-10 G-0242 2057, driven rashly and negligently dashed the motorcycle resulting his death.
The accident was reported to the police station Marwahi, district Bilaspur upon which Crime No. 102/2014 was registered under Section 304(A) of the IPC against the respondent No.1/driver.

A claim case was filed by the appellant/claimant claiming compensation of Rs. 53,50,000/- from the respondents inter alia pleading that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

3. The application was resisted by the respondents on various ground and the learned Tribunal framed issues on the basis of the above pleadings and decided the issue No. 1 and 6 in favour of the appellant/claimant.

The further pleadings of the claim application is that deceased Sonu @ Sunil Kumar was aged about 24 years at the time of accident and was working in the SECL, Korba as a Loader and was earning about Rs. 20,000/- per month.

The offending vehicle was driven by respondent No.1/driver owned by respondent No.2 and insured with the Insurance Company therefore all of them are liable to pay compensation as claimed and stated above.
4. Respondent No.1 & 2/driver and owner of the offending vehicle were proceeded ex-parte and did not file any written statement.

Respondent No.3/Insurance Company filed its written statement and Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5314 barring the admitted fact denied the remaining averments of the claim application with regard to age, profession, monthly income etc.

It was further pleaded that the offending vehicle was being used in violation of terms and conditions of the Insurance policy therefore without any valid permit, fitness and driving license therefore the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
5. Learned Tribunal framed as many as seven issues on the basis of the above broad pleadings.

Issue No.1 and 2 with regard to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent No.1/driver was decided in favour of the appellant/claimant and issue No.3 with regard to violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance policy was decided in favour of the appellants/claimants.
Issue No.3 is with regard to the contributory negligence and it was decided not proved.
Issue No.5 is with regard to fastening of liability upon the parties is also decided as not proved.
Issue No.5 and 6 is with regard to the relief and cost, the learned Tribunal was pleased to award Rs. 12,64,880/- as total compensation in favour of the appellant/claimant.

6. Shri Agrawal, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company submits that the income of the deceased was proved as Rs. 15,960/- by leading evidence and on the basis of which,

the findings so recorded cannot be said to be perverse or contrary to the record.
He further submits that though 30% future prospect is awarded on the income of the deceased but under other heads sufficient amount has been awarded therefore it does not require any interference.

7. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the records.
8.

The findings recorded by the learned Tribunal appears to have been based upon proper appreciation of evidence brought on record therefore Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5314 such finding cannot be said to be in the opinion of the court perverse or contrary to the records.
The Tribunal has taken the monthly income of the deceased to be Rs. 15,960/- and after deduction of 50% as personal income it would come to Rs. 7,980//-.
However, the Tribunal has taken the age of the mother of the deceased instead of the age of the deceased and has applied the multiplier of 13.

The yearly income to Rs. 95,760/- and after applying the multiplier of 13 which would come to Rs.
12,44,880/-.
The appellant/claimant is the mother of the deceased and therefore under the conventional heads i.e. Filial consortium of Rs. 10,000/-, funeral expenses of Rs. 10,000/- have been added.
Thus, the Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs. 12,64,000/-.
9. Now comes as to whether just compensation has been awarded or not.

Considering the evidence available on record, nature of job, number of dependents, this Court reassess the compensation as under:
10.

The deceased was a government employee, learned Tribunal has taken the monthly income of the deceased is taken to Rs. 15,960/- (as per the salary slip Ex.A-9) and 50% future prospect is added which comes to Rs. 7,980/- (Rs. 15,960/-x 50%) and after addition, the monthly income would come to Rs. 23,940/- and yearly income comes to Rs. 2,87,280/-.
After deducting 1/2 income, which would come to Rs. 1,43,640/- (Rs.2,87,280/2 = Rs. 1,43,640/-) and the yearly dependency would come to Rs. 1,43,640/-.

The appellant/claimant is the mother of the deceased and sole claimant and instead of taking the age of the deceased which is 24 years, the learned Tribunal has wrongly assessed the multiplier of 13 by taking the age of the mother which is 50 years,

therefore after applying the multiplier of 18, the amount on loss of dependency would come to Rs.
25,85,520/- (Rs. 1,43,640/-x18).

After adding Rs. 70,000/- (Rs. 15,000/- for funeral expenses, Rs.
15,000/- for loss of estate and Rs. 40,000/- as filial Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5314 loss of consortium) under other admissible heads, the total compensation would come to Rs. 26,55,520/-.
11.
The learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 12,64,880/- and after reassessing by this Court, the appellants are entitled to receive compensation of Rs. 26,55,520/-.
If any amount is deposited earlier, the same shall be adjusted.

After deducting the amount awarded, the enhanced amount would be Rs. 13,90,640/- to be paid to the appellant/claimant which shall carry interest @
6% from the date of claim application till its realization.
The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the enhanced amount with interest within a period of 60 days.
12. Appeal is thus, partly allowed.
